In Williamson County, deeds and other real property records are recorded by the county clerk, and the clerk's page lists where to search them. This guide gives the office details and recording rules we could confirm on official pages. We did not confirm every fee or hour, and we say where we could not.

Where to find Williamson County property records

The Williamson County clerk's page describes Official Public Records covering land titles, liens, releases of liens, plats, IRS liens, trusts, security agreements, restrictions and notices.

  • Office: County Clerk.
  • Address: 1848 Texas Trail, Georgetown, TX 78626 (recording and vital records).
  • Phone: 512-943-1515.
  • Hours: Research Library, Recording and Vitals: 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., Monday to Friday.
  • Online records search: official records search.

The clerk's office says it does not perform searches for the public.

What Texas law says about recording

The county clerk serves as the county recorder, and deeds and other instruments are recorded in the county where the property is located (Local Government Code Sec. 191.001). The clerk must correctly record instruments that are proved, acknowledged or sworn to, in the order filed (Property Code Sec. 11.004).

A deed for real property executed after December 31, 1981 must show a mailing address for each grantee, or the filer pays a penalty fee equal to the greater of $25 or twice the statutory recording fee (Sec. 11.003). See Texas property records and the warranty deed and quitclaim deed guides.

The county clerk, who serves as the county recorder (Local Government Code Sec. 191.001).

Where do I search Williamson County property records?

Use the clerk's online records search linked above.

What must a deed show to be recorded?

It must be acknowledged or sworn, and show each grantee's mailing address or the filer pays a penalty fee (Property Code Sec. 11.003).

Can I sell a house with a title or lien problem?

Yes. The title company pays recorded liens from the proceeds at closing, and we buy houses as-is.

  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See how we buy houses in Texas.

King County property records FAQ

Who records deeds in King County?

The county clerk, who serves as the county recorder (Local Government Code Sec. 191.001).

Where do I search King County property records?

Use the clerk's online records search linked above.

What must a deed show to be recorded?

It must be acknowledged or sworn, and show each grantee's mailing address or the filer pays a penalty fee (Property Code Sec. 11.003).

Can I sell a house with a title or lien problem?

Yes. The title company pays recorded liens from the proceeds at closing, and we buy houses as-is.
